---
title: "PreCheck: An AI-Assisted Tool and Evaluation Framework for Preregistration Quality"
---
**Presenter:** Bence Palfi, Goldsmiths, University of London

**Co-authors:** Zoltan Kekecs (Eötvös Loránd University), Dominik Dianovics (Eötvös Loránd University), Jamie Cummins (University of Bern), Balazs Aczel (Eötvös Loránd University)

### Abstract {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Preregistration is widely recognised as a cornerstone of transparent and reproducible research, yet producing and evaluating high-quality preregistrations remains resource-intensive and inconsistent. In this poster, we introduce PreCheck, an AI-powered tool developed by the ResearchCheck Collaboration to support researchers by automatically reviewing preregistrations and providing structured, actionable feedback. PreCheck is designed to reduce workload burden on researchers and reviewers while improving the clarity, completeness, and credibility of research plans across behavioral and the life sciences.

PreCheck utilises a novel, domain-general evaluation framework that integrates and simplifies existing preregistration assessment approaches. The tool evaluates preregistrations across seven key dimensions (e.g., sample size and statistical methods specification, inference criteria), with a particular focus on detecting analytic flexibility and vagueness in research plans, and generates actionable recommendations to improve rigor.

We also present the first comprehensive validation study of PreCheck, addressing a central barrier to adopting AI tools in scientific workflows: lack of trust. Using our framework, we conducted a large-scale expert validation involving more than 60 preregistrations of psychology projects sourced from Open Science Framework via random sampling procedure. Each preregistration was independently assessed by three human raters, enabling robust estimates of inter-rater reliability and the creation of a high-quality benchmark dataset. We further evaluated PreCheck through systematic agreement tests across multiple LLMs and parameter settings, examining consistency between automated and expert judgments as well as sensitivity to modeling choices.

Together, this work addresses the "last mile" problem of AI adoption in science by combining tool development with transparent, multi-method validation. PreCheck provides scalable support for preregistration while establishing a generalisable framework for evaluating similar tools, contributing to more credible and reproducible research practices.
